text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria may not need to import wheat this year because this year's crop is expected to meet fully domestic consumption, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power plant said it would switch off one of its 1,000 megawatt reactors today for planned repairs. @
-- Bulgaria will not waive a cooking oil export fee of $90 per tonne because of an expected low sunflower seed crop this year, an Agriculture Ministry official said.

-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutor's Office has issued an arrest warrant for Bulgaria's former communist deputy Prime Minister Ognyan Doinov on charges of fraud, officials from the National Investigation Servise said.

-- Payments through VISA credit cards were halted in Bulgaria after the central bank waived its permision to the private Bank For Agricultural Credit (BAC) to service VISA cards, state BTA news agency said. BAC was declared insolvent by the Sofia City Court on July 18.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would raise its main annual interest rate to 5.59 percent from 5.50 percent, effective Monday.
